value:
The Earth Federation Forces are victorious in the battle at Odessa.
In order to regrow in the domain of space, they begin rebuilding the space military complex Jaburo.

Meanwhile, several Zeon units band together— aiming to bounce back from their shortcomings on land— and commence a major attack on Jaburo.

The Earth Federation Forces begin Operation Cembalo with Space Fortress Solomon set as their target.

The operation's success would rely on the use of the Federation's secret weapon, the Solar System.
However, Dozle Zabi's merciless monster enters the battlefield...

The EFF manage to subjugate their enemy at Solomon.
Thus, they initiate Operation Star One—the plan to attack the very heart of Zeon.

However, they find themselves in unprecedented danger when they lose one third of their main forces after being hit by Zeon's Solar Ray.

Despite their now-insufficient fighting power, the Federation Forces attempt a desperate rush for a triumphant conclusion at A Baoa Qu.

After a grueling success breaking through their enemy's defense line at A Baoa Qu, victory seems within reach for the Federation.

As countless lives are lost on the battlefield, Amuro and Char clash in a fight that would end their rivalry.
After an intense battle, A Baoa Qu falls; the unprecedented conflict that claimed half of humanity results in victory for the Earth Federation Forces.

The mobile suits fielded in this war were truly a game changer, fundamentally modifying the dynamics of the battlefield.

Lacking mobile suits of their own, the Federation Forces were overwhelmed by Zeon at the outset of the war, but the development and deployment of the legendary Gundam provided the catalyst for a counteroffensive.

With the new mobile suit among its assets, the White Base Corps moved from battlefield to battlefield, earning one victory after another. These exploits, preserved in history, became symbols of the Federation's triumph.

It would be no exaggeration to credit the Federation Forces' successful development and employment of mobile suits as the decisive factor in Zeon's downfall.

***

Amuro Ray of the White Base Corps—with his rare talent— makes considerable gains on the battlefield until his Gundam's reaction speed begins failing
to keep pace with his awareness.

Meanwhile, Challia Bull, a Newtype fighting for Zeon, unleashes an assault on the White Base.

During the One Year War, individuals possessing superhuman perception and intuition known as Newtypes emerged, and the Zeon army was the first to attempt weaponizing their talents.

Zeon advanced the development of custom mobile weapons to maximize Newtype abilities, and in the final stages of the One Year War, succeeded in deploying these machines in combat.

The large mobile armor Braw-Bro was one such example.
With its fierce all-range attacks, it caused the Gundam to overheat, putting the White Base on the back foot.
It was nevertheless destroyed by Amuro Ray, who finally awakened as a Newtype.

Had the Gundam overheated earlier than it did in established history, the timeline might well have branched in a different direction.
Operation Star One, Part 1– The G-3 Gundam

As the battle rages on at A Baoa Qu, Amuro enters in resonance with his allies, and their Newtype abilities begin to awaken.

A new mobile suit arrives— as decided by the Federation's leadership— to replace the broken Gundam at the White Base.
Operation Star One, Part 2 – Vs. Newtype

The pilots of the White Base Corps now possess their full Newtype power.

The Zeon forces acknowledge the danger and decide to send their most elite fleet to battle the White Base Corps.

After the fiery encounter, A Baoa Qu falls.
The White Base Corps is considered heroic for its distinguished and valiant feat.
The Rise and Fall of Newtypes

In this alternative timeline, Newtype abilities spread, and multiple pilots on the White Base awakened as Newtypes in rapid succession.

Truly, the way they understand one another without words embodied the human potential inherent to Newtypes, the new form of humanity.

Unfortunately, given the harsh realities of wartime, this power was only ever seen as a tool for combat.

As a result, the true nature of Newtypes was never understood, and these individuals soon faded from history following the war.

In preparation for the final battle, the Federation Forces task the White Base Corps with a diversionary mission.

The White Base Corps deploys ahead of the Federation's main forces and finds itself being chased by its arch enemy Char Aznable.

Designated the 13th Independent Unit and tasked with serving as a decoy, the White Base Corps found itself under relentless assault from Zeon the moment it cleared the atmosphere.

The attack was spearheaded by Captain Char Aznable, the White Base's deadly nemesis.

In addition to commanding the Zanzibar, he mobilized the Camel Patrol Fleet, setting up multiple layers of encirclement.

However, the White Base—battle-hardened by repeated life-and-death engagements—had already transformed into an elite fighting force.

Bolstered by Amuro Ray's awakening as a Newtype, the White Base managed to repel its pursuer even in a severely damaged state.

Thus, the White Base fulfilled its role as a decoy.
And yet, had the White Base achieved even greater results on the battlefield, the course of history might well have changed.

The diversion is considered a success. In preparation for the White Base's next target, Solomon, the Gundam receives upgrades and repairs.

Although the Gundam receives a considerable upgrade in its firepower, the repairs remain incomplete. Its unaddressed decline in mobility leaves Amuro visibly concerned.

He puts his worries aside as the great battle at Space Fortress Solomon is set to begin.
Operation Star One – The Hidden Actor

After a crushing victory at Solomon, the Earth Federation Forces endeavor to sustain their momentum by heading to Side 3 and commencing a follow-up attack.

On the other side, some members of the Zeon forces begin having trepidations over the imminent fight.

Gihren fires the Solar Ray, wiping out the Federation Forces' fleet.
This should have turned the tables of war in Zeon's favor.

Under Amuro Ray's leadership, the survivors advance toward Zeon's headquarters with intentions to fell the evil dictator corrupting outer space.

With the Zabi family now eliminated, the One Year War comes to an end.

General Revil is entrusted with postwar reconstruction.
He—having seen humanity's potential on the battlefield— makes an important decision to build a world that bridges the gap between Earth and space.

In this alternative timeline, Amuro Ray—awakened as a Newtype—used his resonating power to reach out to the combatants on the battlefield in a life-saving miracle that crossed the divide of friend and foe.

General Revil was saved by this miracle, and following the war, led the Federation government as an exceptional statesman.

After completing the reconstruction of the devastated colonies, he resumed the long-suspended space emigration program, charting a course that balanced preserving the Earth's environment with expanding humanity's biosphere.

This action marked the decisive first step humanity took toward its next stage.

When compared to established history, it is easy to imagine that humanity grasped a brighter future in this timeline.

The Principality of Zeon suffers a deciding loss in the battle on Earth's surface.

But after discovering the entrance to the Federation Forces' general headquarters, Jaburo, they are presented with a rare opportunity to regain the upper hand.

The remaining units on Earth band together and begin their operation to invade Jaburo.

In space, the Earth Federation Forces move forward to attack Space Fortress Solomon, a key base for the Principality of Zeon.

Zeon's defenses are crushed by their enemy's formidable new weapon, leaving the commander Dozle Zabi no recourse but to abandon the fortress.

The giant mobile armor Big Zam is deployed to destroy itself against the enemy fleet and allows the surviving units to escape.
Defense of A Baoa Qu, Part 1

After Solomon falls, the Federation advances further to attack A Baoa Qu, a base of vital importance to Zeon.

Zeon's supreme commander, Gihren Zabi, fires his army's ultimate weapon, the Solar Ray, eliminating the Federation's main fleet and killing his own father, Degwin.

The Federation is now vulnerable after suffering such a heavy loss.
A confident smile spreads across Gihren's face as he gives his next order.
Defense of A Baoa Qu, Part 2

The defending army takes the advantage under Gihren's baton, until the situation takes a sudden turn for the worse.

The Zeon forces fall into temporary disarray after Supreme Commander Gihren is assassinated by Kycilia.

In the face of complete collapse, the only thing supporting the army's morale is its devotion to its nation.

A Baoa Qu has fallen, and the Zabi family is eliminated.
The Principality of Zeon has lost all ability to resist the Earth Federation Forces, and the curtain closes on the war that lasted an entire year.

Although Zeon raised the banner of space-emigrant independence, the war it started was in truth a reckless overreach by the Zabi dictatorship.

Consequently, the war not only claimed the lives of Earthnoids, but also of their fellow Spacenoids, culminating in an unprecedented calamity that wiped out half of the total population.

Worse still, it deepened the divide between the two sides, becoming the source of endless conflicts to come.

Had Zeon produced an influential leader outside of the Zabi bloodline, the timeline might well have branched in another direction.

As the final battle draws near after the fall of Solomon, Captain M'Quve sets a trap at Texas Colony in order to settle a score with a certain enemy Gundam.

Meanwhile, Char is granted a new mobile unit and prepares to confront the Gundam.

Dark clouds loom over Texas Colony as a fearsome battle opposing the three becomes imminent.

As commander of the Odessa base, M'Quve oversaw the supply of mineral resources from Earth to the homeland and led the relief fleet during the Battle of Solomon, earning him the trust of the Zeon leadership—specifically, Kycilia.

Making up for his many defeats was not the only reason he personally challenged the Gundam in a mobile suit.
It was also an attempt to win back Kycilia's favor from Char.

Indeed, when Char interfered, M'Quve drove him off the battlefield, determined to destroy the Gundam on his own.

In the end, M'Quve's life was cut short by the Gundam, but had a strategic thinker of his caliber survived, the timeline might well have branched in a different direction.
Defense of A Baoa Qu, Part 1 – The United Maintenance Plan

M'Quve is promoted to vice admiral after wresting control over the battle in Texas.
He continues progress of the United Maintenance Plan as preparations are made for the final battle against the Earth Federation Forces.

With the high-performance unit entrusted to him by M'Quve, Char challenges the approaching Gundam.
Defense of A Baoa Qu, Part 2 – A Link to a New Day

Against the Federation's overwhelming numbers, Zeon's defenses begin to crumble at A Baoa Qu.

As defeat becomes seemingly inevitable, M'Quve makes a plan to withdraw to Axis to salvage Zeon's chances to recover.

Char, having grasped M'Quve's ulterior motives, places himself at the rear of the retreat.

A Baoa Qu falls, spelling a loss for the Principality of Zeon.

However, M'Quve and Char, along with numerous officers, set off for Axis, where hopes for recovery lie.

In this alternative timeline, Zeon's defeat remained inevitable.

And yet, together, M'Quve and Char succeeded in defeating their nemesis, the Gundam.
With the survival of so many of its soldiers, Zeon retained its military influence, which ultimately shaped the Federation government's postwar policies.

The war came to an end. However, allowing Zeon maintain its military might carried the risk that a misstep by either side could easily reignite the conflict.

May a calamity eclipsing even the One Year War never visit humanity in this timeline.

Strike on the Mobile Suit Factory

The operation at Jaburo ends in failure and Zeon's army suffers tremendous losses.

Yet, in the midst of the chaos, a construction unit led by Char Aznable manages to infiltrate the base.

Having lost its foothold on Earth, Zeon's assault on the Federation Forces' headquarters at Jaburo was a last-ditch gamble to reverse the course of the war.

However, even after locating the secret entrance to the base and mobilizing its full might for an assault on the base, it failed to bring down the impregnable fortress.

In the end, both the full-scale assault from above and the covert sabotage from within were thwarted, sealing Zeon's fate in the Earth Sphere.

Had Zeon managed to damage the mobile suit factories, spaceship docks, and other base functions vital to the Federation's later operations, the timeline might well have branched in a different direction.

As a result of the events that took place in Jaburo, the Federation is forced to delay the invasion.

The Principality of Zeon uses the time gained to fortify its defenses.

After his success at Jaburo, Char pilots his new machine back toward Solomon.
Defense of A Baoa Qu – The Perfect Zeong

Having delayed the Earth Federation Forces' plan of invasion, the Principality of Zeon seizes the chance to build a unit designed for a Newtype to pilot.

The final battle has come.
The Zeon army assumes its positions at A Baoa Qu, fully prepared to fend off the invading Earth Federation Forces.

After a gruesome battle, A Baoa Qu remains standing.
The Zeon army then devises a plan to recapture Solomon.

Char pilots the Perfect Zeong, and alongside Lalah and Challia, moves toward the enemy front lines where Amuro waits.

The year is U.C. 0080.
The Newtypes at Solomon attain a resonance that transcends speech itself.

The Principality of Zeon succeeds in retaking Solomon.

But its success comes at a great cost; both armies are now battered to the extent that they have to accept a ceasefire.

In the ongoing confusion, a single hero takes the stage and reveals their true name.

In this alternative timeline, Zeon repelled the Federation Forces' offensive and secured its long-sought independence.

This victory was made possible not only by the deployment of multiple weapons absent from the historical record, but also by steadily eroding the Federation's military strength across multiple fronts.

Although Kycilia's death plunged postwar society into chaos, Casval emerged as its new leader.
Proclaiming the reformation of humanity, he led a war-torn world into the future.

The new world he set forth could lead to a complete revision of Universal Century history.
Fight Zeon now that it has optimized its combat readiness.

While examining records from U.C. 0079, the simulator uncovered information on the White Base crew's non-combat activities during their time on Earth.

Although they found themselves on the front lines time and again, the brief intervals separating battles may have afforded them respite from the conflict, where they could take in the natural beauty of the Earth.

Those moments in which they set aside their roles as soldiers and allowed themselves to enjoy fleeting moments of leisure illustrate the preciousness of ordinary life.
Fight the EFF now that they have optimized their combat readiness.

While examining records from U.C. 0079, the simulator uncovered information on a young Newtype in the Zeon forces.

Discovered by Char Aznable for her talent while on Earth, she demonstrated exceptional resonating power, becoming a personal support of his, both in public and in private.

Her end was tragic, but her spirit endured, imprinting itself in the minds of two Newtypes with whom she shared a deep connection— Char Aznable and Amuro Ray—and profoundly influencing their future actions.

Observational data from U.C. 0079 has been fully examined.

While the simulator has finished examining these alternative timelines based on the investigative results, collecting more extensive observational data will likely enable examination of further historical branching points and possibilities.

May the data uncovered by this examination serve as a guide for the development of this world and the path that humanity ought to take.

In this alternative timeline, Operation Cembalo, the Federation Forces' assault on Solomon, ended in an overwhelming victory that far surpassed the historical one.

As a result, the White Base managed to avoid the tragedy that struck them in established history.

Surviving the battle, Sleggar Law not only continued to support the front lines as an experienced soldier, but also became a source of strength for his younger comrades, boosting the ship's morale.

Furthermore, it goes without saying how great the joy of Mirai Yashima—who had wished from the bottom of her heart for his return—must have been.

In this alternative timeline, the two Newtypes named Lalah Sune and Challia Bull made significant contributions to winning the war under their commander, Char Aznable.

Surviving the battles that had sealed their fate in established history, they continued to stand by Char's side even after the war, maintaining their support for him in all aspects of his life.

Their Newtype abilities—once exploited solely for combat—were transformed by the arrival of peace into a light that illuminated new avenues for humanity's potential.

That brilliance would serve as a guidepost for striving toward a better world.
